newsitem.title: USA: G7 upbeat on world economy, sees faster growth.
newsitem.headline: G7 upbeat on world economy, sees faster growth.

text.p: The Group of Seven industrial nations on Saturday delivered an upbeat assessment of the outlook for the world economy, saying inflation was low and forecasting faster growth into 1997.
In a statement issued to reporters after a nearly six-hour meeting, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the powerful group also welcomed recent movements in currency markets.

"We welcomed developments in exchange markets over the recent period," Rubin, who acted as chairman of the meeting, said in his statement. "And we reaffirmed our standing commitment to reduce (trade) imbalances and to cooperate closely in the exchange markets."
The dollar has been buoyant in recent days, although for the most part currency rates have been broadly stable for some time.
Rubin said the G7 finance ministers and central bankers generally believed that the world economy had improved since their last meeting in April and looked forward to even better times ahead.
The G7 is comprised of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
